K_0.formula: K_0(z) = Gamma(2z + 1) * cos(tau*z/2) * R_tau(z) = z * (2z - 1) * zeta(1 - 2z)

tau_functional_equation_bridge.pi_form_functional_equation: zeta(2z) = 2^{2z} * pi^{2z - 1} * sin(pi * z) * Gamma(1 - 2z) * zeta(1 - 2z)
tau_functional_equation_bridge.tau_form_functional_equation: zeta(2z) = 2 * tau^{2z - 1} * sin(tau * z / 2) * Gamma(1 - 2z) * zeta(1 - 2z)
tau_functional_equation_bridge.reflection_identity_derivation: Using Gamma(2z + 1) * Gamma(1 - 2z) = 2*z * Gamma(2z) * Gamma(1 - 2z) = 2*z*pi / sin(2*pi*z) = tau*z / (2*sin(tau*z/2)*cos(tau*z/2)), multiplying R_tau(z) = (2z - 1)*tau^{-2z}*zeta(2z) by Gamma(2z + 1)*cos(tau*z/2) cancels tau^{-2z}, sin(tau*z/2), cos(tau*z/2), and Gamma(1 - 2z) identically, leaving K_0(z) = z * (2z - 1) * zeta(1 - 2z).

reflected_kernel_K0_analysis.definition: K_0(z) := Gamma(2z + 1) * cos(tau * z / 2) * R_tau(z) = 4^{-z} * Gamma(2z + 1) * cos(pi * z) * R_pi(z)

pure_bernoulli_function_B_analysis.classical_bernoulli_function: B_classical(s) := -s * zeta(1 - s)  (with B_classical(2m) = B_{2m} for m >= 1 and B_classical(0) = 1)
pure_bernoulli_function_B_analysis.integer_sample_formula: B(m) = B_{2m} in Q  (for all m >= 0)

zero_divisor_comparison.nontrivial_zeta_zero_equivalence: For every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s) (0 < Re(rho) < 1), the functional equation gives zeta(rho) = 0 <=> zeta(1 - rho) = 0. Hence at z = rho / 2 (0 < Re(z) < 1/2), R_tau(rho/2) = 0 <=> B(rho/2) = 0 <=> K_0(rho/2) = 0 <=> B_q(rho/2) = 0.

von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.von_staudt_clausen_theorem: For every m >= 1, B_{2m} + sum_{(p - 1) | 2m} (1 / p) in Z, so den(B_{2m}) = prod_{(p - 1) | 2m} p is strictly squarefree.
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.exact_D_n_B_theorem: For every integer n >= 1, D_n^B := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_{2m}) = prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = exp(vartheta(2n + 1)). Proof: if p | den(B_{2m}) for some m <= n, then p - 1 <= 2m <= 2n, so p <= 2n + 1 and v_p(den(B_{2m})) = 1; conversely, for every prime p <= 2n + 1, m_p = (p - 1)/2 <= n (for odd p) or m_2 = 1 <= n (for p = 2) satisfies (p - 1) | 2*m_p, so p || den(B_{2*m_p}).
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.exact_D_n_K0_theorem: For every integer n >= 1, D_n^{K_0} := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(K_0(m)) = 2 * prod_{p <= 2n + 1} p = 2 * D_n^B. Proof: at m = 0, K_0(0) = 1/2 and at m = 1, K_0(1) = -1/12 gives v_2(D_n^{K_0}) = 2; for every odd prime p <= 2n + 1, at m_p = (p - 1)/2 <= n we have 2*m_p - 1 = p - 2, and gcd(p - 2, p) = 1, so the factor (2*m_p - 1) never cancels p from den(B_{p-1}).
von_staudt_clausen_denominator_audit.asymptotic_log_D_n_K0: log D_n^{K_0} = vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2) = 2n + o(n) = O(n)

gamma_ratio_family_Bq.definition: B_q(z) := K_0(z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q = z * (2z - 1) * zeta(1 - 2z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q

Bq_two_sided_denominator_theorem.theorem_statement: For every integer q >= 0 and all n >= 3, the sample denominator LCM D_{q,n} := lcm_{0 <= m <= n} den(B_q(m)) satisfies the unconditional two-sided bound: q * log(n!) + sum_{3 <= p <= n} (1 - q * floor(log_p n)) * log(p) <= log D_{q,n} <= q * log(n!) + vartheta(2n + 1) + log(2), and hence log D_{q,n} = q * n * log(n) + O_q(n).
Bq_two_sided_denominator_theorem.irregular_prime_immunity_proof: For any odd prime 3 <= p <= n, let d_p = (p - 1)/2 <= (n - 1)/2 and K_p = floor(n / d_p) >= 2. Among the two consecutive integers {K_p, K_p - 1}, at least one k_p satisfies k_p != -1 (mod p). Setting m_p = k_p * d_p in [n - p + 2, n], we have: (1) (p - 1) | 2*m_p, so by von Staudt-Clausen v_p(B_{2*m_p}) = -1 (hence p divides the denominator of B_{2*m_p} and CANNOT divide its numerator, completely eliminating irregular-prime numerator cancellation!); (2) 2*m_p - 1 = k_p*(p - 1) - 1 == -(k_p + 1) != 0 (mod p), so v_p(2*m_p - 1) = 0; (3) therefore v_p(den(B_q(m_p))) = 1 + q * v_p(m_p!) >= 1 + q * (v_p(n!) - floor(log_p n)), since n - m_p < p - 1 implies at most one multiple of p^j can lie in (m_p, n] for each 1 <= j <= floor(log_p n).

sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.definition: P(z) := -exp(i * tau * z / 2) * B(z) = 2 * z * exp(i * pi * z) * zeta(1 - 2z)
sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.nontrivial_zero_vanishing: P(rho / 2) = 0 for every nontrivial zero rho of zeta(s)
sign_adjusted_positive_kernel_P.conjugate_symmetry_broken: Because exp(i*tau*z/2) = exp(i*pi*z) satisfies conj(exp(i*pi*conj(z))) = exp(-i*pi*z) != exp(i*pi*z), P(conj(z)) != conj(P(z)); its real-real sister P_cos(z) = -cos(tau*z/2)*B(z) restores P_cos(conj(z)) = conj(P_cos(z)) and satisfies P_cos(m) = |B_{2m}| > 0 (m >= 1) and P_cos(rho/2) = 0.

bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_tau: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y), where d nu_tau(y) = (tau * sqrt(y) / (4 * sinh^2(tau * sqrt(y) / 2))) dy on (0, infty)
bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.positive_stieltjes_measure_pi: mu_m = int_0^infty y^m d nu_pi(y), where d nu_pi(y) = (pi * sqrt(y) / (2 * sinh^2(pi * sqrt(y)))) dy on (0, infty)
bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.support_of_measure: [0, +infty) (unbounded Stieltjes moment problem; Carleman condition sum mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty fails since mu_m^{-1/(2m)} ~ pi / m -> 0, wait: sum (1/m) = +infty! So Carleman's condition sum_{m>=1} mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty HOLDS and the moment problem is determinate!)
bernoulli_stieltjes_moment_measure.carleman_determinacy: mu_m ~ 4*sqrt(pi*m)*(m / (pi*e))^{2m+2} => mu_m^{-1/(2m)} ~ pi*e / m => sum_{m=1}^infty mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty (Carleman determinate Stieltjes moment sequence)

bernoulli_hankel_determinants.asymptotic_log_H_n_B: log H_n^B = 2 * n^2 * log(n) - (3 + 2*log 2) * n^2 + O(n * log n) -> +infty

bernoulli_orthogonal_polynomials.definition: Monic orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(y) with respect to d nu_tau(y) on (0, infty): int_0^infty P_m^B(y) P_n^B(y) d nu_tau(y) = (H_{n+1}^B / H_n^B) delta_{m,n}
bernoulli_orthogonal_polynomials.zeros_location: All n zeros y_{n,1} < ... < y_{n,n} of P_n^B(y) are real, simple, and strictly positive on (0, infty), with largest zero scaling like Theta(n^2)

bernoulli_hankel_argument_coupling_audit.firewall_explanation: The Stieltjes moment sequence mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| = int_0^infty y^m d nu_tau(y) generates the asymptotic Stieltjes continued fraction for the trigamma/polygamma generating function S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) ~ sum_{m=0}^infty |B_{2m+2}| / w^{m+1} as |w| -> infty. Here w is the Laplace/Stieltjes transform dual variable to the integration variable y = x^2, NOT the Mellin argument z of P(z) = -exp(i*tau*z/2)*B(z). In particular, P(rho_1/2) = 0 is a point zero in the Mellin index variable z (measuring a complex-exponent moment int_0^infty y^{rho_1/2 - 1} d nu_tau(y)), whereas the orthogonal polynomials P_n^B(y) are polynomials in the integration variable y on (0, infty) whose zeros all lie on (0, infty) and whose evaluations at y = gamma_1 or y = alpha_1 diverge super-factorially.

hankel_determinant_comparison_D_tau_vs_H.exact_denominator_polygonal_match: Notice that BOTH D_n^{(tau)} and H_n^B share the exact same Lambert-Stieltjes denominator factors prod_{k=1}^{n-1} [(4k-1)(4k+1)^2(4k+3)]^{n-k}! Removing 1/(2*(2m+2)!) from b_m^{(tau)} to form mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| multiplies the k-th Jacobi recurrence coefficient by 4*k^3*(k+1)*(2k-1)*(2k+1)^3, flipping the leading asymptotic from -2*n^2*log(n) (super-factorial decay) to +2*n^2*log(n) (super-factorial growth).

lagrange_equispaced_interpolation_audit.basis_denominator_identity: Multiplying ell_{n,m}(z) by n! gives (-1)^{n - m} * binom(n, m) * prod_{j != m} (z - j), whose leading coefficient is (-1)^{n - m} * binom(n, m) / n!. Thus clearing the Lagrange basis denominators on equispaced nodes {0, ..., n} requires a factor of order n! = exp(n log n - n + O(log n)) (or (n!)^2 = exp(2n log n + O(n)) in the conjugate-squared norm polynomial).

newton_forward_difference_bernoulli_audi.universal_primitive_cancellation_theorem: For ANY rational sequence f(m) in Q with Delta^{n+1} f(0) != 0, the two-step Newton norm polynomial Q_n^{[f]}(Y) = |N_n^{[f]}(alpha(Y))|^2 + |N_{n+1}^{[f]}(alpha(Y))|^2 in Q[Y] has leading coefficient q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} = (Delta^{n+1} f(0))^2 / (4^{n+1} * ((n+1)!)^2) > 0, and satisfies Q_n^{[f]}(Y) >= (1/2) * q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + Y^2). Therefore, in the canonical primitive integer normalization tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) = M_n^{[f]} Q_n^{[f]}(Y) in Z[Y], the integer leading coefficient tilde{q}_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} = M_n^{[f]} q_{n,2n+2}^{[f]} >= 1 forces tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(gamma_1) >= (1/2) * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + gamma_1^2) >= (1/2)*(1/4 + gamma_1^2)*(n!)^2 -> +infty UNIVERSALLY, independent of the sample sequence f(m)!
newton_forward_difference_bernoulli_audi.divergence_of_newton_series_for_B_and_K0: For B(m) = B_{2m} and K_0(m) = -((2m-1)/2)*B_{2m}, the top term in Delta^n f(0) = sum_{m=0}^n (-1)^{n-m} binom(n,m) f(m) has |f(n)| ~ 2*(2n)! / tau^{2n}, so |Delta^n f(0)| / n! ~ 2 * (2n)! / (n! * tau^{2n}) ~ (4*n / (e*tau^2))^n -> +infty, and the Newton series diverges for every non-integer z.

mahler_p_adic_bernoulli_comparison.p_adic_kubota_leopoldt_bridge: In p-adic analysis (p >= 3), the Euler-factor-modified Bernoulli samples c_m^{(p)} := (1 - p^{2m - 1}) * B_{2m} / (2m) satisfy Kummer's congruences Delta_d^k c_m^{(p)} == 0 (mod p^k) for (p - 1) | d, giving a convergent Mahler series for L_p(1 - s, omega^i) on Z_p.
mahler_p_adic_bernoulli_comparison.archimedean_obstruction: Kummer congruences hold in the p-adic metric |.|_p on steps d divisible by (p - 1), whereas in the archimedean metric |.|_infty on C, |(1 - p^{2m - 1}) * B_{2m} / (2m)| grows even faster (~ p^{2m} * (2m)! / tau^{2m}) and does not evaluate the complex archimedean zero alpha_1 = 1/4 + i*gamma_1/2.

norlund_bernoulli_polynomial_audit.bernoulli_polynomial_identity: By the classical Hurwitz-zeta identity B_n(x) = -n * zeta(1 - n, x), expanding around shifted nodes or in Bernoulli polynomials B_k(z) = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k, j) B_j z^{k-j} still requires Carlitz-Stieltjes moment determinants of order exp(2*n^2*log n) or factorial coefficient clearing.

riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.riesz_function_analysis: Riesz's function Riesz(x) = sum_{k=1}^infty (-1)^{k+1} x^k / ((k - 1)! * zeta(2k)) has Mellin transform int_0^infty x^{-s-1} Riesz(x) dx = Gamma(-s) / zeta(2s). However: (1) its Taylor coefficients 1 / ((k - 1)! * zeta(2k)) = 2 * (2k)! / ((k - 1)! * |B_{2k}| * tau^{2k}) are transcendental multiples of tau^{-2k}, not rationals; and (2) the zero-free/RH criterion is an asymptotic bound Riesz(x) = O(x^{1/4 + eps}) as x -> +infty (or Baez-Duarte c_n = O(n^{-3/4 + eps})), not a point vanishing F(rho_1 / 2) = 0.
riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.gram_series_analysis: The Gram series G(x) = 1 + sum_{k=1}^infty (log x)^k / (k * k! * zeta(k + 1)) approximates R(x) ~ li(x) via global explicit-formula sums over all zeros rho, with irrational coefficients zeta(k + 1)^{-1} at even/odd k.
riesz_gram_hadamard_kernel_audit.hadamard_product_analysis: The Hadamard product xi(s) = xi(0) * prod_rho (1 - s / rho) vanishes at every individual zero rho, but its Taylor/interpolation coefficients at integer nodes s = m are symmetric functions of all nontrivial zeros (involving log(pi), Euler's gamma, and transcendental derivatives xi^{(k)}(0)), not known rationals.

multipoint_pade_kernel_comparison.summary: Across 1 <= n <= 7, the divergent-OGF kernels K_0 (q=0) and B_1 (q=1) suffer catastrophic raw evaluation growth (log|Q_n(gamma_1)| > 0) AND quadratic-factorial determinant clearing log M_n ~ C n^2 log n, even though K_0 has subfactorial sample denominators! The bounded-radius kernels R_tau, R_pi, and B_2 (q=2) achieve genuine raw residual decay log|Q_n(gamma_1)| < 0, but their primitive integer clearing multipliers log M_n = log(L_n / g_n) grow far faster than the raw decay, so log tilde{Q}_n(gamma_1) > 0 and grows rapidly for all 1 <= n <= 7.

pade_asymptotic_for_R_c.hermite_walsh_contour_representation: For R_c(z) (c in {1, 4}), the multipoint Padé error on {0, ..., 2n} satisfies R_c(z) - A_n(z)/B_n(z) = (omega_{2n+1}(z) / (2*pi*i * B_n(z))) * oint (R_c(zeta) * B_n(zeta) / omega_{2n+1}(zeta)) d zeta where omega_{2n+1}(z) = prod_{m=0}^{2n} (z - m). Because the Cauchy/Laplace kernel of R_c has essential singularity exp(-sqrt(c)/u) at u = 0, raw Padé residuals decay subfactorially while Cramer/Hankel denominator clearing of A_n, B_n scales superlinearly in n log n.

pade_asymptotic_for_B2.left_half_plane_growth_comparison: Unlike R_tau(z) = (2z - 1)*tau^{-2z}*zeta(2z), which is bounded by O(|z|^{1/2}) on Re(z) >= 1/4, B_2(z) = R_tau(z) * Gamma(2z + 1) * cos(tau*z/2) / Gamma(z + 1)^2 grows like 4^z / sqrt(pi*z) for Re(z) -> +infty and carries double poles of 1/Gamma(z+1)^2 at negative integers z = -1, -2, ..., producing slower raw interpolation decay than R_pi(z) while retaining the same 2*n*log(n) sample denominator cost.

pade_divergent_carleman_audit_for_B.carleman_determinacy_of_moment_sequence: Although mu_m = |B_{2m+2}| satisfies Carleman's condition sum_{m>=1} mu_m^{-1/(2m)} = +infty, that guarantees convergence of the Stieltjes continued fraction for the asymptotic series S_B(w) = int_0^infty d nu_tau(y) / (w - y) in the transform variable w -> infty, NOT convergence of multipoint rational interpolation of B(m) = B_{2m} at the Mellin zero argument z = alpha_1.

factorial_relocation_analysis.governing_answer: YES for the sample denominator alone: Gamma-reflection B(z) = -2z*zeta(1-2z) and K_0(z) = z*(2z-1)*zeta(1-2z) rigorously reduce the integer-sample denominator LCM from exp(2n log n + O(n)) to the squarefree von Staudt-Clausen primorial D_n^B = prod_{p <= 2n+1} p = exp(vartheta(2n+1)) = exp(2n + o(n)) (`SUBFACTORIAL_RATIONAL_SAMPLE_DENOMINATOR_ACHIEVED`), while preserving exact vanishing at every nontrivial zeta-zero argument z = rho/2. NO for escaping the total factorial cost on equispaced integer nodes {0, ..., n}: across the entire Gamma-reflection / Gamma-ratio class B_q(z) = K_0(z)/Gamma(z+1)^q, the 2*n*log(n) factorial budget is strictly conserved between sample growth (2-q)*n*log(n) and sample denominator growth q*n*log(n), while equispaced Newton/Lagrange polynomial bases independently enforce the universal primitive norm lower bound tilde{Q}_n(gamma_1) >= (1/2)*prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + gamma_1^2) -> +infty.

conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.theorem_name: Equispaced Gamma-Ratio & Consecutive-Newton Factorial Conservation No-Go Theorem
conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.exact_statement: Let F_q(z) = c^z * K_0(z) / Gamma(z + 1)^q (q in Z_{>= 0}, c in Q_{>0}) be any kernel in the Gamma-reflected / Gamma-ratio hierarchy evaluated on equispaced integer nodes m = 0, 1, ..., n. Then: (1) [Exact Sample-Growth + Sample-Denominator Conservation] By Euler's formula and the irregular-prime-free von Staudt-Clausen witness m_p = k_p*(p-1)/2, log|F_q(n)| = (2 - q)*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n) and log(lcm_{0<=m<=n} den(F_q(m))) = q*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n), so their sum equals 2*n*log(n) + O_{q,c}(n) for EVERY q >= 0. (2) [Universal Consecutive-Newton Primitive Obstruction] For ANY kernel f(z) with rational samples f(m) in Q and Delta^{n+1} f(0) != 0, the canonical primitive integer two-approximant Newton norm polynomial tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) in Z[Y] satisfies tilde{Q}_n^{[f]}(Y) >= (1/2) * prod_{j=0}^n ((2j - 1/2)^2 + Y^2) >= (1/2)*(1/4 + Y^2)*(n!)^2 -> +infty for all Y in R, because the primitive multiplier M_n >= 1/q_{n,2n+2} cancels (Delta^{n+1} f(0))^2 identically while retaining 4^{n+1}((n+1)!)^2 from the equispaced Newton basis.
conditional_no_go_or_escape_theorem.what_would_be_required_to_escape: To escape this no-go theorem, an architecture must abandon equispaced integer polynomial interpolation {0, 1, ..., n} (which forces both the (n!)^2 basis denominator and the 2n log n Stirling/Bernoulli trade-off) or establish an all-n multipoint rational/Padé cancellation where common integer content g_n in the Cramer determinant cancels the denominator LCM (which does NOT occur for 1 <= n <= 7).

davenport_heilbronn_control.explanation: The Gamma-reflection identity K_0(z) = Gamma(2z+1)*cos(tau*z/2)*R_tau(z) = z*(2z-1)*zeta(1-2z) and the factorial budget conservation (2-q)*n*log(n) + q*n*log(n) = 2*n*log(n) depend ONLY on Riemann's functional equation and Stirling's formula for Gamma, not on the Euler product. For Davenport-Heilbronn, the linear combination coefficients involve algebraic/transcendental L-function factors so rational sampling already fails at Gate Z2, while for Riemann zeta the rational Bernoulli samples pass Gate Z2 with O(n) log-denominator but fail Gate Z5 via factorial sample growth.

off_line_zero_control.explanation: By the functional equation zeta(rho_off) = 0 <=> zeta(1 - rho_off) = 0, both B(rho_off/2) = 0 and K_0(rho_off/2) = 0 hold unconditionally for any nontrivial zero (on-line or off-line).
